analyst_view.overall: Braga (17th, 4 pts) host KuPS (33rd, 1 pt) and need the win to move toward the top 24; no match preview is out yet this far ahead, so this rests on club news. Braga sacked Carlos Vicens on 20 October and new coach Franclim Carvalho has steadied them (2-0 over Gent, 3-0 over Famalicao, a draw at Aarhus), with Ricardo Horta their top scorer in Europe. KuPS' Finnish season ended on 8 November with a 2-0 home loss to Inter Turku; they finished third, won none of their last five and will have gone 18 days without a competitive game by Thursday, something the numbers cannot see. The numbers carry no missing players for either side and already count Braga's heavy recent shot output (+26%). No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, about 2.1 of them Braga's. I lean a little higher: KuPS' league season is over and they arrive after 18 days without a match and five games without a win (3 goals scored, 7 conceded), which the numbers can't see. A mild +4% gives about 2.7 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, about 7 for Braga, already lifted 9% for Braga's recent corner count and cut for KuPS' few. KuPS will mostly defend deep, which the split already reflects, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already trimmed for both sides' recent quiet discipline. A one-sided game against a team defending deep usually stays calm and no referee is named yet, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, already pushed up 26% for Braga's recent shot volume and down for KuPS'. KuPS' rustiness argues for even more Braga pressure, but Braga's busy schedule may bring some rotation, and the numbers already carry a big lift, so I stay at about 29.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, 7.5 of them Braga's. A KuPS side out of season and out of form should give up cleaner chances than usual, which the numbers can't see, so I lean slightly higher: +3% gives about 10.4.
